input.name: one-api-instance
input.problem: one API instance, no load balancer, 10k concurrent users

messages.content: We expect 10,000 concurrent users at launch. Review my design.

output.text:
Thanks - 10k concurrent users is substantial, so we can't afford single points of failure or hitting the main databases too often. The design check found exactly two things to fix now while you're here:

1) "Mobile app" -> "Orders API": direct call with no load balancer. This would fail if that one Orders API instance goes down, and 10k concurrent users will hammer it hard at launch. Fix: add a load balancer in front of the Orders API, then run two instances behind it for redundancy and better load distribution.

2) "Orders API" -> "Orders DB": every read goes straight to the database with no cache in front. With 10k concurrent users that will do reads, the database will be overloaded. Fix: add a cache (like Redis/Memcached) in front of the Orders API so repeat reads hit the cache instead of hitting the main DB.

Proposed changes now:
- Add a load balancer between Mobile app and Orders API. Connect Mobile app to the load balancer, then have the load balancer point back to two different Orders API instances (Orders API and a new one).
- Add a cache node in front of the Orders API for reads.

To make this work: do I add two Orders API nodes? Or should we keep a single strong API instance? Also, what are you doing with the Catalog service and its DB/replica/cache - do those read hits matter too, since they have no cache either (Catalog service -> Catalog cache is there but it's for catalog reads)?

If you say "go ahead", I'll add: 
- a load balancer (call it "Orders LB"), connecting to both API instances
- a cache node ("Orders cache") and linking the Orders API to that so all reads hit cache first.

I need your preference on the API instance count before making the moves.

Let me add the proposed fixes and ask your preference on the API instances first.

I'll add:
1. A load balancer in front of the Orders API
2. A cache for the Orders API reads
3. A second Orders API instance (to run behind the LB)

Let me re-check the board — there is already Catalog cache for catalog reads, which is separate from orders reads. But we need a new cache for Orders API reads:

(I stopped here: that was the most steps I take in one answer. Ask me to continue.)
